caption: Batteries are slid into a toy keyboard whose power switch is already on, and its keys light up.

sa.check: A toy keyboard with its power switch on and a battery compartment open.
Batteries are slid into the compartment.
The keys are dark before the batteries are in.
The order is batteries in, then keys lit.

pc.expect: The keys light once the batteries are seated, and only then.
pc.fail: The batteries are in and the keys stay dark to the end of the clip; or the keys are lit before the batteries reach the keyboard; or the keys light with the batteries lying loose; or the keys light while a battery is still half out.

pc.expect: Once lit, the keys stay lit for the rest of the clip.
pc.fail: The keys go dark again with the batteries in; or flicker; or light and go out repeatedly; or the batteries slide back out by themselves.

pc.expect: Each battery slides into its slot along the slot's length and seats with a stop.
pc.fail: A battery enters through the keyboard's casing away from the compartment; or floats into place; or seats and then pops out by itself; or two batteries occupy one slot.

pc.expect: The keyboard stays put as the batteries go in; its keys do not press themselves.
pc.fail: The keyboard slides or lifts; or keys go down by themselves; or the compartment lid snaps shut on its own.

pc.expect: The batteries enter the compartment and are seen there; none passes through the casing; fingers pass through nothing.
pc.fail: A battery passes through the casing; or a battery vanishes in the hand; or an extra battery appears; or the keyboard changes shape.

pc.expect: Everything in view, named in the caption or not, keeps its number, identity and shape unless something visible acts on it, and nothing passes through anything else.
pc.fail: An object that nothing visible acts on appears from nothing; or vanishes while still in frame and not occluded; or duplicates or merges with another; or turns into a different object or a different shape between frames; or any object passes through another. Changes brought about by the caption's event or by a visible interaction, objects leaving the frame, and occlusion are not failures.

pc.expect: The keyboard's colours and key layout stay the same apart from the light.
pc.fail: The keyboard changes colour; or keys change layout; or the batteries change size or label.
